blocks.text: Smoke Management Systems
Controlling smoke, protecting escape routes, saving lives.
Call Now

We design and implement comprehensive smoke management systems (also known as smoke ventilation systems) that control the movement of smoke during a fire event, protecting evacuation routes and enabling safe egress for building occupants. Our Civil Defence approved solutions — including smoke extraction, staircase pressurization, and fire damper installations — are engineered in accordance with NFPA 92, BS EN 12101, and ADCD/local authority requirements. From high-rise residential towers to large commercial complexes across Abu Dhabi and the UAE, we deliver fully integrated systems that work in coordination with fire detection and suppression infrastructure.

blocks.text: Fire Dampers

Fire dampers work alongside smoke extraction and pressurization as part of a complete smoke management strategy, automatically sealing duct penetrations to stop fire and smoke spreading between compartments through the HVAC system itself. A building can have strong smoke extraction in one zone, but if unsealed ductwork lets smoke travel into another compartment, that containment strategy has failed at the exact point it was meant to hold. We supply, install, and maintain Civil Defence approved fire dampers across Abu Dhabi and the UAE — see our Fire Dampers page for full detail on types, standards, and installation.

blocks.alt: Staircase pressurization fan system maintaining smoke-free escape stairwell in Abu Dhabi

blocks.text: Staircase Pressurization Fans

Staircase pressurization systems maintain a higher air pressure within escape stairwells compared to the rest of the building, preventing smoke infiltration and keeping evacuation routes clear during a fire. We engineer and install dedicated pressurization fan units with automatic control systems that maintain precise pressure differentials as required by NFPA 92 and local civil defense standards. Our designs account for door-opening forces, building height, and leakage paths to ensure consistent, code-compliant performance under real fire conditions.Learn more about staircase pressurization fans →

blocks.text: Fresh Air Fans

Fresh air fans play a critical dual role in buildings — supporting everyday ventilation for occupant comfort while integrating into the smoke management strategy during emergency scenarios. We design systems that introduce controlled volumes of clean outside air into occupied spaces, corridors, and refuge areas in compliance with ASHRAE and local mechanical codes. Each installation is balanced and commissioned to ensure proper airflow distribution across all building zones under both normal and emergency operating modes.

blocks.text: Make-Up Air Fans

Make-up air fans replenish the air exhausted by smoke extraction systems, preventing negative pressure build-up that would otherwise reduce extraction effectiveness and compromise fire door operation. Our engineers carefully calculate the required make-up air volumes for each zone to maintain balanced smoke ventilation system performance throughout a fire event. These units are installed with appropriate fire ratings and interlocked with the overall smoke control sequence to activate automatically in response to fire alarm signals.

blocks.text: Kitchen Ventilation Systems

Commercial kitchen ventilation systems require specialist design to manage high volumes of grease-laden air, heat, and cooking fumes while meeting strict fire safety and hygiene standards. We supply and install complete kitchen exhaust and supply air systems, including grease filters, UV systems, and fire suppression-ready ductwork, fully compliant with NFPA 96 and local authority requirements. Our solutions are designed for longevity and ease of maintenance, reducing grease accumulation risk and ensuring safe, code-compliant kitchen operations. Learn more about our kitchen ventilation systems→

blocks.text: Smoke Extraction Fans

Smoke extraction fans remove smoke from a building during a fire, keeping escape routes, stairwells, and common areas clear enough for safe evacuation and emergency response. As part of a complete smoke management system, they activate automatically on a fire alarm signal, drawing smoke away from occupied areas before it can spread and obscure exit paths or trigger toxic inhalation risks. We supply, install, and maintain Civil Defence approved smoke extraction fans across Abu Dhabi and the UAE, with regular testing ensuring reliable operation and full compliance with fire safety standards.
Where Smoke Management Systems Are Required

Smoke management systems are a mandatory Civil Defence requirement across a wide range of building types in Abu Dhabi and the UAE, particularly where evacuation routes need to stay clear of smoke long enough for occupants to exit safely. We design and install compliant smoke management and smoke ventilation systems for:

items: High-rise residential towers — protecting stairwells and corridors with pressurization systems
Commercial and office buildings — extraction and make-up air systems integrated with fire alarm systems
Basement car parks — smoke extraction to maintain visibility and breathable conditions during evacuation
Shopping malls and large retail spaces — zoned smoke control systems for complex, multi-level layouts
Hospitals and healthcare facilities — specialized systems accounting for non-ambulatory occupants and phased evacuation
Industrial and warehouse facilities — high-capacity extraction for large open floor plates

What Happens If You Don't Have a Compliant Smoke Management System

A non-compliant or poorly maintained smoke management system doesn't just increase fire risk — it can bring an entire project to a halt. Buildings without a properly functioning smoke management system (or smoke ventilation system, as it's also known) commonly fail Civil Defence inspection, delaying occupancy certificates and handover at the worst possible stage of a project. Many insurers also require proof of a compliant, maintained fire and smoke system before honoring claims related to fire incidents, leaving building owners exposed if their system isn't up to standard. Beyond the paperwork, the real risk is to occupants — without proper smoke extraction and pressurization, evacuation routes fill with smoke faster, reducing the time available for safe egress. Fixing a non-compliant smoke management system after a failed inspection is almost always more costly and time-sensitive than getting the design and installation right from the start, and building owners can ultimately be held liable for injuries or damage linked to a system that wasn't compliant or functioning as required. The good news is that all of this is preventable — our team can assess your current smoke management system, or help you design one that's fully compliant before it becomes a problem at handover.
Smoke Management System — Frequently Asked Questions

items.q: What is a smoke management system?
items.a: A smoke management system — also known as a smoke ventilation system — is a set of engineered mechanical systems including extraction fans, pressurization units, and ductwork, designed to control the spread of smoke during a fire and keep evacuation routes clear so occupants can exit safely. It works alongside fire detection and suppression systems as part of a building's overall fire safety strategy.

items.q: Is a smoke management system mandatory in Abu Dhabi and the UAE?
items.a: Yes. Civil Defence authorities across Abu Dhabi and the UAE require smoke management systems in most commercial, residential, and high-rise buildings as part of fire safety compliance. Requirements vary depending on building type, height, and occupancy — our team can assess what's required for your specific project.

items.q: What standards do your smoke management systems comply with?
items.a: Our smoke management and smoke ventilation systems are engineered in accordance with NFPA 92, BS EN 12101, and local Civil Defence and DOE requirements, ensuring full regulatory compliance across Abu Dhabi and the UAE.

items.q: What's the difference between smoke extraction and staircase pressurization?
items.a: Smoke extraction actively removes smoke from a space, typically corridors or basements, while staircase pressurization keeps escape stairwells at a higher air pressure to prevent smoke from entering in the first place. Both are core components of a smoke ventilation system, and most buildings require them working together as one coordinated system.

items.q: How much does a smoke management system cost?
items.a: Cost depends on building size, occupancy type, and system complexity. Contact our team for a free assessment and quote tailored to your project.

items.q: Do you provide maintenance for existing smoke management systems?
items.a: Yes, we offer Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) for smoke management and smoke ventilation systems, including inspection, testing, and rectification to keep your system compliant and fully operational.
